detaileddescription.para: Injects one fault per unique node per iteration. Measures pure registry insertion throughput on the fast path (no expiry, no callbacks).
Queries a single permanently-active fault. Measures the per-call cost of the mutex-protected hash-map lookup on the hot path.
Gate: average latency ≤ 1 µs. Gate threshold emitted as counter.
Injects a fault then immediately recovers it; measures the inject+recover round-trip cost as a proxy for recover throughput.

briefdescription.para: GATE-CHS-04 — Concurrent inject + query throughput (8 threads).

detaileddescription.para: Four inject threads and four query threads run concurrently against the same FaultInjector. Measures combined ops/s.
Enqueues entries with a far-future trigger_at while the scheduler is stopped to measure pure queue-insertion throughput without firing overhead.
Compares injectFault() throughput with 0 callbacks (baseline) vs. 10 callbacks registered. Gate: ratio ≤ 2× (measured externally from JSON output).
Parameterised via state.range(0) = number of callbacks.

briefdescription.para: Release gate benchmarks for the chaos framework (Phase 5 hardening delivery).

detaileddescription.para: Validates six hard performance gates for the chaos runtime hot paths:

GATE-CHS-01 injectFault() single-threaded throughput ≥ 500 000 ops/s GATE-CHS-02 isFaultActive() query latency ≤ 1 µs average per call (positive path) GATE-CHS-03 recoverFault() single-threaded throughput ≥ 200 000 ops/s GATE-CHS-04 concurrent inject+query (8 threads) ≥ 200 000 ops/s combined GATE-CHS-05 ChaosScheduler schedule() throughput ≥ 100 000 entries/s GATE-CHS-06 event callback dispatch overhead ≤ 2× baseline (10 callbacks vs 0)
Gate thresholds are emitted as benchmark counters so CI tooling can validate results from the JSON output: bench_chaos_release_gates benchmark_format=json benchmark_out=gates.json
